learning_outcomes.text: Explain how machine-learning models are applied to diagnostic tasks at a conceptual level
Describe common data types used in diagnostic AI, such as images and structured records
Interpret evaluation metrics including sensitivity, specificity and AUC conceptually
Explain why AI outputs are decision-support that require clinician confirmation, never a standalone diagnosis
Identify sources of bias, dataset shift and failure modes in diagnostic models
Summarise the regulatory, safety and ethical considerations for diagnostic AI

integrative_case: A health-informatics student evaluates, as a classroom exercise, a described diagnostic-support model: they interpret its sensitivity and specificity, flag a likely dataset-shift risk, and write a short note explaining that any model output must be confirmed by a qualified clinician before it informs care.
assesses: knowledge and applied reasoning on every in-scope outcome via MCQ/MR
case-based decisions in the integrative case
